book.title: Empire of Pain
book.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
book.subtitle: The Secret History of the Sackler Dynasty

characters.name: Isaac Sackler
characters.shortBio: Immigrated to Brooklyn from Galicia in the early 1900s. Ran a grocery store in Flatbush that failed during the Great Depression. Fiercely valued education.
bullets: Immigrated from Galicia (modern-day Poland/Ukraine) in the pre-WWI wave
Settled in Flatbush, Brooklyn
Ran a grocery store that was wiped out by the Depression
Despite poverty, insisted all three sons pursue medicine
The family's financial precariousness shaped the brothers' relentless ambition

characters.name: Sophie Sackler
characters.shortBio: Born Sophie Greenberg. Mother of the three Sackler brothers. Eastern European Jewish immigrant. Partner in Isaac's dream of upward mobility through education.
bullets: Born Sophie Greenberg
Eastern European Jewish immigrant background
Raised three sons who all became physicians
Endured the Depression-era collapse of the family grocery store

characters.name: Arthur M. Sackler
characters.shortBio: The architect of the Sackler empire. Physician, psychiatrist, art collector, and the man who invented modern pharmaceutical advertising. Funded his brothers' educations and built the playbook Purdue Pharma would later use for OxyContin.
bullets: Eldest of the three brothers — quasi-paternal figure to Mortimer and Raymond
Worked multiple jobs to put his brothers through medical school
Worked at Creedmoor State Hospital in Queens doing psychiatric research
Acquired William Douglas McAdams, a medical advertising agency
Invented modern pharma marketing: direct-to-physician campaigns, broadening indications, KOL strategy
Masterminded the Valium campaign for Roche — made it the first $100M drug
Founded the Medical Tribune, a widely-read medical newspaper
Had a stake in IMS Health — tracked prescription data, giving him unmatched market intelligence
Prolific art collector: Sackler Wing at the Met, galleries at the Smithsonian
Married three times: Else Jorgensen, Marietta Lutze, Jillian Tully
Died before OxyContin existed — but built the machine that made it possible

characters.name: Mortimer D. Sackler
characters.shortBio: The middle brother. Physician. More reserved than Arthur. Co-purchased Purdue Frederick Company with Raymond in 1952. Eventually relocated to London.
bullets: Middle brother — quieter, more reserved than Arthur
Education funded by Arthur's relentless hustle
Co-purchased Purdue Frederick Company with Raymond in 1952
Relocated to Europe, based in London
Involved in Purdue's international operations

characters.name: Raymond R. Sackler
characters.shortBio: The youngest Sackler brother. Physician. Worked closely with Mortimer in the pharmaceutical business. Co-purchased Purdue Frederick Company.
bullets: Youngest of the three brothers
Also became a physician, funded by Arthur
Co-purchased Purdue Frederick Company with Mortimer in 1952
Worked closely with Mortimer on the business side

characters.name: Else Jorgensen
characters.shortBio: Arthur Sackler's first wife. They married in the early 1940s. The marriage ended in divorce.
bullets: Married Arthur in the early 1940s
Marriage ended in divorce

characters.name: Marietta Lutze
characters.shortBio: Arthur Sackler's second wife. Also ended in divorce.

characters.name: Jillian Tully Sackler
characters.shortBio: Arthur's third and final wife. Significantly younger. Became the primary steward of his art collection, philanthropic legacy, and reputation after his death.

notes.title: The Immigrant Story
notes.content: The Sacklers are a classic American immigrant family — Galician Jews who arrived in Brooklyn with nothing. Isaac's grocery store failed in the Depression, but the family's obsession with education as the path out of poverty would produce three doctors in one generation.

notes.title: Arthur the Engine
notes.content: Arthur is the protagonist of the early book. He's not just ambitious — he's operating on a different level. Working at Creedmoor while simultaneously building an advertising empire. He essentially funds his brothers' entire medical education. The dynamic between the brothers is almost feudal: Arthur as lord, Mortimer and Raymond as beneficiaries.

notes.title: The Playbook
notes.content: This is where the book's thesis crystallizes. Arthur doesn't just advertise drugs — he invents the system. Direct-to-physician marketing, broadening indications beyond clinical evidence, using KOLs, owning the data pipeline (IMS Health). The Valium campaign is the proof of concept. Everything Purdue later does with OxyContin is Arthur's playbook, perfected.
